program: Lung health education, school asthma response, research and policy

what: Respiratory Health Association provides lung-health education and works on asthma, COPD, tobacco and air quality.
Its school asthma work helps staff prepare for respiratory emergencies with training, equipment and rescue medication.
Research, caregiver support and policy advocacy complement those practical services.
strengths: Prompt asthma response offers a concrete acute health mechanism.
School staff training and stocked medication can reach students before emergency escalation.
Current institutional reporting and original returns make implementation scale and costs inspectable.
reservations: Cumulative medication uses and reported avoided ER visits are not a causal annual outcome estimate.
State funding, school nurses and existing inhalers materially constrain donor additionality.
Local household resources, outside payer costs and marginal funding capacity are unknown.

sections.what: Respiratory Health Association, EIN 36-2222687, is the whole recipient for education, research, policy and events. RESCUE Illinois Schools supplies medication, equipment and training with state support; statewide eligibility intersects Chicago counties but does not prove their actual caseload. This model uses a hypothetical Chicago local branch, not all Illinois outcomes. [Current asthma programs](https://resphealth.org/asthma-programs/)
sections.monitoring: The official page reports over 2,500 staff trained, more than 3,000 schools supplied,1,172 medication uses and 360 claimed avoidedERvisits. These are cumulative program reports with unclear counterfactual ascertainment and no local annual unique denominator. Uses, return to class and alleged avoidedERvisits are not deaths prevented or causal QALYs. Obtain distinctChicago students/households, respiratory severity, actual alternateinhaleraccess, repeatedevents, emergencyvisits and parentcare/work outcomes.
sections.qualitative: Prompt albuterol and prepared staff plausibly shorten or prevent escalation of acute distress, but effectiveness depends on timely use, clinical appropriateness and available alternative medication. This bounded initial review found no local causal health-utility measurement. The 500 localHH, .2 incremental improvement, .25 annual-package response and .003 QALY per avertedacuteevent are explicit judgments. .003 means about 1.1 healthyday, once; no futuredeath/survivorwage credit or chronic annual utility is inferred. State appropriations and schoolimplementation already exist in the counterfactual; advocacy is not retroactively credited with all publicprogrambenefits. Other lung/policy/research effects are unpriced, notzero.

sections.funding:
The 2025 original reports governmentgrants$1,337,733 and netassets$1,661,969. Theofficial programhistory says 2023 stateappropriation$2.4 M launchedRESCUE and 2024 renewal supportedit; these are already-funded publicalternatives, not additionaldonoroutputs. Currentavailability does not demonstrate freshunfundedcapacity or latestcontractrenewal. Anordinarygift goes to thewholeRHArecipient; request a pricedincrementalworkplan, schoolgeography andreplacementfunding. [History](https://resphealth.org/about-us/our-successes/) [Giving](https://resphealth.org/support-us/)

Root independently checked the current Illinois grant listing: $535,000 for RHA in July 2026–June 2027, with health and economic absenteeism/cost-savings evaluation requirements. This is a current funded baseline and an evaluation plan, not realized clinical or cash outcomes. The official July 2025–June 2026 report describes vaping education and the $25 inhaler copay law effective January 1, 2026; those existing policy benefits remain outside this incremental acute branch.
